'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Attacks on refugee camps in the Gaza war#Nuseirat|Attacks on refugee camps in the Gaza war]], [[Killing of health workers in the Gaza war]]
****A [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]] reportedly kills a [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] medic at the [[Nuseirat refugee camp]] in the central [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/israeli-strikes-in-gaza-said-to-kill-medic-high-school-student-no-immediate-idf-comment/ (Reuters via ''The Times of Israel'')]

[https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5299973-israel-kills-senior-hamas-led-police-official-gaza-medics-and-police-officials (''Asharq Al-Awsat'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-kills-senior-hamas-led-police-official-gaza-medics-police-officials-say-2026-07-25/ (Reuters)]

**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy|naval forces]] of the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] claims to have stopped four vessels from transiting the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/irans-irgc-says-four-vessels-stopped-hormuz-last-24-hours (''Middle East Eye'')]
***[[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran]]
****[[Ministry of Health and Medical Education|Iranian health ministry]] spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour reports no [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] strikes against [[Iran]], after 13 consecutive nights of [[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran|strikes]] by the [[United States Central Command|U.S. Central Command]] against the country. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/iran-reports-no-us-strikes-overnight-tensions-remain-high-rcna589191 (NBC News)]
****The [[United States]] halts strikes against Iran after [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|government]] officials reportedly saw a potential opening to resume diplomatic efforts and [[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations|talks]]. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/07/us-halts-strikes-iran-sees-opening-talks-what-know (Al-Monitor)] [https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-trump-diplomacy-netanyahu-d491158a4c9a1d3429a87a6ed58f2f72 (AP)]
**[[Red Sea crisis]], [[Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war]]
***Two people are injured by [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led coalition [[airstrike]]s on [[Hodeidah]], [[Houthi-controlled Yemen]]. A [[Patriot (missile)|Patriot]] battery operated by the [[Hellenic Armed Forces|Greek military]] intercepts two [[ballistic missile]]s fired by the [[Houthis]] at [[Aramco]] facilities in [[Yanbu]] and [[Jizan]], Saudi Arabia. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/25/saudi-military-strikes-iran-backed-houthi-targets-yemen.html (CNBC)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/middle-east/yemens-houthis-fire-missiles-drones-saudi-arabia-response-strikes-rcna589200 (NBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/26/new-front-in-us-iran-war-escalates-as-houthis-fire-at-saudi-oil-facilities (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] officials say a [[Russia]]n [[Drone warfare|drone strike]] on a [[Ukrposhta|postal facility]] in [[Sumy]] has killed two people. [https://www.bgnes.com/conflicts/two-killed-in-drone-strike-on-ukrainian-city-of-sumy (AFP via BGNES)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***[[Darfur Joint Protection Force]] spokesperson Mutawakkil Ali Wakil confirms that, in coordination with the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] (SAF), that the joint force have retaken control of [[Umm Sayala]], [[North Kordofan]], [[Sudan]], with 38 members of the [[Rapid Support Forces]] confirmed to have been killed. [https://sudanhorizon.com/joint-forces-spokesman-capture-of-umm-sayala-cuts-militia-supply-route-defections-hasten-victory/ (''Sudan Horizon'')]
***The SAF and Darfur Joint Protection Force recapture [[Jebrat al Sheikh District|Jebrat al Sheikh]] alongside the North Kordofan towns of [[Barah, Sudan|Bara]] and Al-Baraka. Additionally, [[Darfur]] [[Darfur Regional Government|governor]] [[Minni Minnawi|Minni Arko Minawi]] confirms the recaptures. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316601 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

**The death toll from the [[Floods in India|flash floods]] in [[Assam]], [[India]], rises to 62, after fourteen more fatalities are confirmed. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/assam-flood-death-count-rises-to-62-over-7-lakh-people-affected-across-12-districts-11819493 (NDTV)]

*Two people are killed when a [[Tecnam P2010]] aircraft crashes into a home in [[Ganderkesee]], [[Lower Saxony]], [[Germany]]. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/article/3361848/1-dead-after-small-plane-crashes-house-germany (DPA via ''South China Morning Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–United States relations]]
**[[Brazil]] denies [[Visa policy of Brazil|visas]] to two [[U.S. state department]] officials seeking [[2026 Brazilian general election|election]]-related meetings in [[Brasília]], citing risks of "political exploitation". The U.S. state department says the visit concerns [[electoral integrity]] and [[freedom of expression]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2652314/amp (AFP via ''Arab News'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Berlin Pride attack]]
**Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old Lebanese-German, drives into a crowd at the [[Berlin Pride|pride festival]] in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], killing a person and injuring 29 others. A suspect is on the run. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/07/25/europe/berlin-pride-car-intl-latam (CNN)]
 
'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Brazilian general election]]
**Brazil's [[Liberal Party (Brazil, 2006)|Liberal Party]] formally nominates [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]] [[Federal Senate (Brazil)|senator]] [[Flávio Bolsonaro]], former [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]]'s son, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming election. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/332443/brazils-right-wing-party-nominates-bolsonaro-son-to-battle-lula (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')] [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/flavio-bolsonaro-launches-brazil-presidential-campaign-touts-support-milei-2026-07-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests]]
**[[Minister of Education (India)|Indian education minister]] [[Dharmendra Pradhan]] resigns after protests over alleged [[2026 NEET controversy|entrance-examination leaks]] and broader [[Education in India|education-system]] irregularities. His resignation marks the [[Modi government]]'s first major concession to the demonstrations. [https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/07/25/india-education-minister-announces-resignation-after-countrywide-protests_6755822_4.html (AFP via ''Le Monde'')]
*The [[Bishop of Aberdeen]] in [[Scotland]] declares the [[sedevacantism|sedevacantist]] [[Sons of the Most Holy Redeemer]] religious institute, an order [[SSPX-affiliated religious orders|associated]] with the [[Society of Saint Pius X]], to be [[excommunication in the Catholic Church|excommunicated]], after they [[consecration of a bishop|consecrated]] a [[bishop (Catholic Church)|bishop]] without [[Holy See|Vatican]] approval. [https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/26410592.conservative-orkney-monks-excommunicated-catholic-church/ (''The Herald'')] [https://thecatholicherald.com/article/founder-of-latin-mass-order-consecrated-sedevacantist-bishop-and-excommunicated (''The Catholic Herald'')]
